## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components, combined with parallel range-merge respawn, can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 11.241 ns/p at N=4000 to 7.979 at N=16000 — pure overhead amortization below the L2 spill point (N≈58254). Crucially, the curve stays FLAT across the L2→DRAM transition: 7.979 at N=16000 (L2-resident, 1.15 MB) versus 7.831 at N=65000 (just past spill, 4.68 MB) and 7.823 at N=262000 (18.9 MB in DRAM). There is no cache-spill knee. A slight rise to 8.095 at N=1000000 likely reflects TLB pressure at 72 MB working set. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve at low q: q=0.05 mirrors q=0.01 but ~0.7 ns/p higher. At q=0.25 the shape breaks — cost RISES from 10.079 at N=16000 to 12.25 at N=4000000, indicating churn overhead grows with N rather than amortizing.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.2 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 36.5% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound at small N (6.4 GB/s at N=4000), transitions to a steady bandwidth-limited regime by N=16000 (9.02 GB/s), but never approaches the ceiling. Death rate degrades the plateau: q=0.05 peaks at 8.35 GB/s (33.1%), q=0.25 at 7.14 GB/s (28.3%). The far-from-ceiling gap is not explained by DRAM latency — the L2-spill transition is flat — but by the codegen characteristics described below.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: the histogram shows zero vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar — `fmul`, `fadd`, `fsub` on individual `s` registers, with `ldp s5, s6` loading component pairs as scalar floats rather than NEON lanes. The inner loop processes one particle at a time, computing grid indices via `fcvtzs`/`csel` clamping and then scattering to a pixel buffer through `ldrb`/`strb` pairs (12 `ldrb`, 16 `strb` in the histogram) — three byte loads, three byte stores, and three `csel` clamps per particle's RGB update. These byte-granular scatter stores cannot coalesce into cache-line writes, which explains why bandwidth plateaus at 36.5% of ceiling rather than approaching it. The `bl` calls to `phase1Range` and `spawn`, plus `___ulock_wait`/`___ulock_wake`, confirm the parallel-merge structure is present but orthogonal to the vectorization failure.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler emitted zero vector instructions, and peak bandwidth is 9.2 GB/s at q=0.01 (36.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling), far from the streaming ceiling the hypothesis predicted. The scalar `fmul`/`fadd` pipeline and byte-granular `strb` scatter stores cap achievable bandwidth regardless of death rate; at q=0.25 the floor drops further to 7.14 GB/s (28.3%) as branchy respawn overhead grows with N. Auto-vectorization did not occur, so the hypothesis cannot hold in any regime.
